text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd has received a multi-option, unsecured debt facility of A$600 million with a seven year amortising term, to help the company stabilise its finances. Finance director Gary Scanlon said the company would use the money to fund its three main gold developments, but he would not rule out a possible share issue to offset the costs. Page 19.

Australis Media managing director Sean O'Halloran has revealed the pay-TV operator had decided by June, after plans to merge with Optus sank, that a zero-growth strategy was the best option to preserve its cash position, and had virtually stopped pushing for new subscribers. Page 19.

Energy Equity Corporation Ltd managing director Maurice Brand said the company would integrate its fuel power projects in Queensland and capitalise on the strategic location of its gas reserves by spending A$48 million on increasing its Barcaldine power sation, developing its gas fields and constructing more gas pipelines. Page 20.

Tony Larkin has returned to BHP Co Ltd as corporate treasurer to replace Tim Knott, now BHP Petroleum group general manager of administration and finance. Larkin was previously working on secondment as senior vice president of finance and investor relations at Foster's Brewing Group, but was always expected to return to BHP. Page 20.

The Australian Securities Commission has applied to its Corporations and Securities Panel to declare New Zealand investor Brierley Investments Ltd's increased stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd as unacceptable conduct, after Brierley lifted its shareholding to almost 23 per cent in June through a swap agreement with Merrill Lynch (Australia) Futures. Page 22.

Apparel manufacturer and importer Gazal Corporation recorded a 55.6 per cent increase in its full-year profit in 1996-97, despite a slight decrease in revenue. Managing director Michael Gazal said yesterday decreased tariffs would make it difficult to maitain local production, but said the company would try to keep around 30 per cent of its manufacturing in Australia. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Seven Australian automotive parts and tooling manufacturers are negotiating joint ventures with Thai partners following a visit to the country last month, when the Australian Automotive Export Group identified potential sales of A$20 million per year, which would almost double the Australian industry's exports to Thailand. Page 29.

Rio Tinto has postponed its planned A$120 million Kintyre uranium mine in north-west Western Australia, which would have been the first greenfields uranium mine in 10 years. The project has been delayed due to falling uranium prices and delays in obtaining native title approval, although there are no substantial conflicts between the company and Aborigines. Page 29.

The Federal Government is examining a policy that could see A$12 billion to A$15 billion of the business in the A$20 billion of oil and gas development in Commonwealth waters under consideration in the next five years go to Australian manufacturers. The proposal would particularly help metal manufacturing companies in Victoria and South Australia. Page 31.

Federal Trade Minister Tim Fischer last week announced he would set up a unit in the trade negotiations section of his department to develop an intellectual property policy to prevent international pirating of the biotech and information industries' ideas ahead of a review of international trading agreements in three years. Page 31.

Victorian Industry Minister Mark Birrell said yesterday the Federal Government's extension of tariffs on the car industry until 2005 had cleared the way for A$1 billion in investment which would focus on design, research, and development in the car and fod industries. Toyota is expected to announce a multi-million facility for the State today. Page 31.

Faulding chief executive Ed Tweddell said yesterday a new Federal Government pricing mechanism for drugs and therapeutic goods, threatened more than A$350 million of pharmaceutical research investment per year. Industry sources claim research in co-operatve centres relying on pharmaceutical industry funding could be withdrawn. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Lend lease has moved 96 per cent of its assets in Australia to 66 per cent as it works towards a global strategy which includes joint ventures and interest diversification. Property director for Lend Lease David Higgins does not expect property profits to come in a big way before 1999 despite recent wins in property contracts, including the Olympic Village and the State Office Block. Page 37.

Victorian Police Commander Allen Bowles, who has been involved in the Victorian Major Fraud Squad, is now to enter the private sector beginning a consultation business for corporations to assist in the prevention of white-collar organised crime. He is entering the private sector after a KPMG survey showed Australian companies suffer millions of dollars worth of fraud each year. Page 39.

A new strategy for the buying and streamlining of company practices in wheat stocks has been introduced by Goodman Fielder who wants to implement a new commodity sourcing project policy called El Nino. The company has also reduced its wheat exposure by 60per cent through the sale of its European Meneba operations. Page 39.

Analysts have said pressure on the lending profit margin in the banking industry is unlikely to effect the Commonwealth Bank's profitability. Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray was feeling the pressure on interest competition betweenbanks last week but believes the Commonwealth will survive because of its high rate on return on equity. Page 39.

Colonial State Bank's managing director Stuart James has said suggestions that Colonial Bank's credit standards have been compromised in order to achieve growth in home lending approvals are untrue. James has admitted that the Bank has began a policy of chasing home loan customers to invest with the State Bank and the funds management business allowed the bank to offer lower home loan rates. Page 39.

UK power station group PowerGen is expected to invest an estimated A$42 million in one of the three major Australian power stations including Pacific power, Delta or Macquarie all of which are part of the New South Wales plan to privatise. Industry source say PowerGen's plans involve the Yallourn partners including Itochu Corporation and AMP. Page 39.
THE AGE

Car manufacturing industry giant Toyota will today give details of its blueprint for Australian operations including the starting date for the manufacture of the new Avalon passenger car. Toyota's operations head Hiroshi Okuda will launch the new plans inMelbourne and it is expected production at its Altona site will be boosted by the introduction of the Avalon scheme. Page B1.

Victorian Police Commander Allen Bowles is to retire from the Victorian major fraud squad and set up his private company aimed at consulting private business and corporations over white-collar crime including fraud. The move comes after a KPMG survey foun that Australian companies lost an estimated A$15 billion dollars in fraud each year and were sometimes unaware of the loss. PageB1.

ANZ is winning in the credit card competition stakes but new customers are forced to pay off credit card balances each month. At a briefing which took place on Friday, ANZ chief general manager Charles Carbonaro said the bank was issuing 268,000 cards each year which has given ANZ a 25 per cent market share in card spending. Page B3.

United States visiting outplacement expert Craig Sawin says one of the biggest challenges in Australian business for the next five years will be to become more economical in the workplace with fewer employees. As the Drake Beam Morin chief executive officr Sawin said Melbourne businesses have cut management by 50 per cent over the past 10 years but continuous streamlining is needed. Page B3.

The Franchise Association of Australia and New Zealand is expected to impose tougher standards on its members in order to protect the public. From September the organisation will expect an adherence to the new code including full disclosure of relevant inormation, a seven day cooling off period for franchisees and compulsory mediation to dissolve disputes. Page B2

Winners of the Victorian franchisee awards Carol and Barry Bird of Braeside Dryton drycleaners took the 1997 Citibank Victoria and Tasmania Service Franchisee of the Year award for their efforts to maintain customers by extending warrantees and giving cusomers a personal touch. Page B2.
